prompt: For a genuinely normal distribution, about 95% of observations lie within two standard deviations of the mean. If standard deviation doubles while the mean stays fixed, what happens to this central band?

options.explanation: A normal distribution has tails outside any finite band.

options.text: Its distance from the mean doubles on each side.
options.explanation: The same standardised distance corresponds to twice the original-unit spread.

options.text: Its width stays fixed because the mean is unchanged.
options.explanation: The mean sets the centre, not the spread.

options.text: It becomes a 95% confidence interval for the mean.
options.explanation: A band of individual observations is different from uncertainty about an estimated mean.

workedExample: Keep the centre and spread separate. The normal percentage belongs to a distance measured in standard deviations. Increasing the unit of spread widens the corresponding original-unit interval.
